TITLE: Internal Status Update: Project Nolaor and Project Soramis

Project Nolaor, which carries the audit finding ID XC-1856-X, continues to be a central focus for the team. Staffed by 30 people, the project has been actively engaged in refining internal controls and addressing documentation inconsistencies. The team has made progress in implementing procedural updates, and feedback from the internal audit team has been incorporated into the most recent deliverables. These adjustments are intended to ensure full alignment with current compliance standards.

Project Soramis is progressing as planned and remains on track for its anticipated completion in Q3 FY26. The project has transitioned from the planning phase into the early stages of execution. Key stakeholders have expressed satisfaction with the project’s direction, and interdepartmental coordination has improved. The project aims to improve supply chain performance, and early modeling efforts have confirmed that the proposed changes are well-positioned to achieve long-term cost optimization goals.

Liluan Nemlurel is leading the development of demand forecasting models under Project Soramis. Her work has provided valuable insights into seasonal purchasing patterns, which have directly informed more accurate inventory planning. Liluan is also working with the finance lead to align the model outputs with the Q3 FY26 budgeting process, ensuring that financial planning reflects the strategic assumptions of the project.

Risk management remains a key priority for both initiatives. For Project Nolaor, the team is closely monitoring the availability of compliance subject matter experts. A limited resource pool could impact the timeline for finalizing the audit response deliverables. To address this, the project team has engaged with the compliance department to explore ways to secure additional support and has scheduled a meeting with the finance team to assess any potential budget impacts.

In the case of Project Soramis, the primary risk is the potential delay in the delivery of custom software tools from the current vendor. Although the project remains on schedule, the team is preparing contingency plans to address any possible disruptions. The project lead is also in early discussions with alternative vendors to ensure that the project maintains flexibility.

In terms of next steps, Project Nolaor will host a workshop at the end of the quarter to finalize the audit response framework. This session will involve representatives from the compliance and operations teams and is intended to ensure that the response fully satisfies the requirements of the internal audit team.

For Project Soramis, the upcoming focus will be on preparing for the pilot phase, which is expected to begin in mid-Q3 FY26. In the coming weeks, the team will work on drafting testing protocols and obtaining necessary stakeholder approvals to move forward.

Liluan Nemlurel will continue to refine the forecasting models and will present updated findings in the next budget review. She is also preparing a technical overview for internal stakeholders, which will be shared for feedback and further refinement.

Both projects remain on solid footing, with teams working diligently to meet objectives and manage risks. Continued collaboration across departments and proactive risk mitigation will be essential to maintaining this momentum.
